technique_why: Paint-along, back to front: a misty wood with clear layers of depth (haze, far trees, ground, near birches), the beginner approach with v2 rules.
subject: An autumn birch wood: a leaf-covered path winding back into a misty blue grove, framed by white birch trunks on both sides under a golden canopy, with a low sun glowing through the trees at the upper left.
focal_point: Where the path disappears into the blue mist between the far firs, with the mossy rock beside it, framed by the near birch trunks.
light: A low sun at the upper left, behind the trees, shining down and to the right through the haze: rays fan out from it, the trunks are lit on their left sides and shaded on their right, and the leaves are brightest toward the sun.
why: Lay the whole misty backdrop first, warm at the sun and blue at the right, then the far woods and rays while everything is soft and simple. Next the ground and the wood's golden leaves, the rock, and only then the birches, which are the subject and get four steps of their own. The fallen leaves go on over the trunks' feet, and the last lights on the rock, the bark and the leaves finish it, all on the sun's side.

things.name: The misty sky and glow
things.why: The whole background is one soft gradient, warm gold at the sun and misty blue toward the right and down, blended wet in one go and run to the bottom edge behind everything.

things.name: The sun
things.why: A small flat pale disk with no lit or shadow side.

things.name: The far misty firs
things.why: Dark firs right of the path and a hazy fir line low on the left: stamped pines, far away, so no light-side taps.
things.left_out: The light side of the far firs: they stay one soft value so they sit back in the mist.

things.name: The far pale birch trunks
things.why: Thin far trunks in the mist, pulled in one stroke each. The element pulls the dark of the wood; these far birches are pale, so the pull is in a pale gray-white and they get no bark marks, since far things get no texture.
things.left_out: Bark marks on the far trunks.

things.name: The sun rays and haze
things.why: Rays of haze dry-brushed over the backdrop and far woods are mist painted on a sky that's already there; only the first step, since rays have no tops to light.
things.left_out: Lit tops and bright edges: rays are soft haze with no form.

things.name: The forest floor
things.why: The ground is a field-like area laid in with horizontal strokes, darker in front; its texture comes from the fallen leaves, so the grass texture step is left out.
things.left_out: Grass texture: the ground is covered in leaves instead, painted as their own thing.
things.called: the bare forest floor, orange gold at the back and rust brown in front, with no leaves on it

things.name: The winding path
things.why: A warm dirt track narrowing back to one point at the far trees, wide at the bottom of the canvas. The element is for strips between rows; this is a single winding strip, so only the pull toward one point is used, and its light comes from the sunlit leaves dabbed on it later.
things.left_out: The edge shading of the path: the fallen leaves cover its edges.

things.name: The golden birch canopy
things.why: Masses of autumn leaves across the top and down the left, built dark to light with dabs, brightest toward the sun.
things.left_out: Single leaf shapes: the canopy is dabs, not drawn leaves.

things.name: The yellow bushes along the path
things.why: Low bushes on both sides of the path and at the foot of the far woods: a leaf mass, olive dark first, then gold, then a few sunlit taps.
things.plain: the dark bushes along the path

things.name: The mossy rock
things.why: A low boulder right of the path with a lit mossy top and a blue-gray shadow side, built from a simple dome shape.
things.left_out: The small dry grass tuft in front of the rock.

things.name: The near birch trunks
things.why: Five white birch trunks (three leaning on the left, two on the right) are the subject: pale trunk, shade, dark bark marks, then light on the sun's side.

things.name: The dark branches
things.why: The dark branches forking from the near birches up into the canopy, pulled thick at the trunk and tapering out.
things.left_out: Fine twigs: only the main branches, so the canopy stays simple.

things.name: The carpet of fallen leaves
things.why: The ground and path are covered in leaves in a mass: a dark pass, two warmer passes each covering less, then sunlit taps, small and close at the back and bigger in front.
things.plain: the dark fallen leaves, with no bright ones among them

paints.name: Pale gold
paints.looks: a pale warm yellow, the glow around the sun (golden yellow plus white)

paints.name: Warm white
paints.looks: white with a touch of yellow, the lightest color in the picture (pale gold plus more white)

paints.name: Misty blue
paints.looks: a soft gray-blue, the mist on the right and the far haze (white, ultramarine, a touch of burnt sienna)

paints.name: Deep blue-green
paints.looks: a dark cool blue-green, the far firs (ultramarine, yellow, a touch of burnt sienna)

paints.name: Gray-white
paints.looks: a pale cool gray-white, the bark of the birches (white with a touch of ultramarine and burnt sienna)

paints.name: Gray-brown
paints.looks: a soft gray-brown, the shaded side of the trunks (gray-white plus a little bark dark)

paints.name: Bark dark
paints.looks: a warm near-black, the bark marks and branches (burnt sienna and ultramarine)

paints.name: Rust brown
paints.looks: a warm red-brown, the bare ground under the leaves (burnt sienna, a little red, a touch of blue)

paints.name: Deep rust
paints.looks: a dark red-brown, the shadowed leaves and the trunks' shadows on the ground (rust brown plus bark dark)

paints.name: Warm tan
paints.looks: a light warm sandy brown, the path (rust brown plus white and a little yellow)

paints.name: Orange gold
paints.looks: a deep orange-gold, the darker autumn leaves (yellow, a little red, a touch of burnt sienna)

paints.name: Golden yellow
paints.looks: a rich warm yellow, the main color of the leaves (yellow with a touch of red and white)

paints.name: Olive
paints.looks: a muted yellow-green, the bushes in shade and the moss on the rock (yellow, a little ultramarine and burnt sienna)

steps.name: Blend the misty glow

lays.what: the whole canvas, top to bottom: pale gold around the sun at the upper left, fading through pale gray-blue to misty blue on the right and toward the bottom

steps.after: The whole canvas is a soft, slightly criss-crossed gradient: warm pale gold in the upper left, cooling through pale gray-blue to misty blue on the right side and the lower half. No white canvas shows.
steps.why: Everything else sits in this haze; running it to the bottom means no white peeks between leaves or trunks later.

steps.name: Circle in the sun

lays.what: the pale sun disk in the upper left, in the middle of the gold glow

steps.after: A small, soft-edged near-white disk glows in the upper left of the gold area. The rest of the backdrop is unchanged.

stages.name: The far woods in the mist

steps.name: Stamp the far misty firs

lays.what: the dark firs rising right of center behind where the path ends, and a lower, paler fir line along the left in the haze

steps.after: Dark blue-green fir shapes stand right of center, pointed at the top and widening down, fading into the mist at their feet; a paler, softer row of firs sits low on the left. The glow and sun are untouched above.
steps.why: The farthest solid things, so they go on first; more misty blue on the left so they sit further back.

steps.name: Pull the far pale trunks

lays.what: six or so thin pale birch trunks standing in the mist in the middle distance, some over the firs, thin and straight, fading out at the bottom

steps.after: Thin, soft, pale gray-white trunks stand in the middle of the canvas, light against the dark firs and barely showing against the pale mist. They have no marks.
steps.why: These sit in front of the firs and behind everything else.

steps.name: Dry-brush the sun rays

lays.what: broad soft rays fanning down and to the right from the sun over the left half of the backdrop, the far firs and the far trunks

steps.after: Broken, see-through bands of pale gold fan out from the sun across the left half, hazing over the far firs and trunks so the left side glows. The right side stays cool blue.
steps.why: The haze has to go over the far woods to push them back, and before the near trees, which stand in front of it.

steps.name: Lay in the forest floor

lays.what: the bottom third of the canvas, rising to a point at the far trees: orange gold at the back, rust brown toward the front

steps.after: The lower third is a warm flat ground, orange-gold at the back where it meets the mist and rust brown toward the bottom edge. The far trees' feet now stand on it. No leaves yet.
steps.why: Only after the far woods: the ground runs up over their base.

steps.name: Pull in the winding path

lays.what: the path from the bottom middle of the canvas narrowing back to a point just left of the far firs, curving a little to the right

steps.after: A light sandy strip runs from wide at the bottom middle to a thin point in the middle distance, where the floor meets the mist. Rust brown ground stays on both sides of it.
steps.why: The path sets the depth the whole picture leads into, so it goes in early and plain.

steps.name: Dab the dark canopy leaves

lays.what: the leaf masses across the top of the canvas and down the left side around the sun, in loose clumps with gaps of sky between

steps.after: Loose orange-gold clumps hang across the top and down the left side, with gaps where the gold glow and blue sky show through. The sun stays clear.
steps.why: The canopy sits behind the near trunks, so its darks go on before them.

steps.name: Dab the dark of the bushes

lays.what: low bushes on both sides of the path, at the foot of the far firs, and along the left where the ground meets the haze

steps.after: Low olive and dark blue-green clumps sit along both sides of the path where it meets the far woods, darkest under the firs. The path stays open between them.
steps.why: The bushes' darks go on before their gold, the same way as the canopy.

steps.name: Dab the golden leaves

lays.what: golden yellow over most of each canopy clump, more toward the sun, the orange showing underneath and on the side away from the sun
golden yellow over the tops of the bushes, more on the left, the olive showing at their feet

steps.after: The canopy and bushes turn golden: yellow over most of each clump, the orange or olive still showing underneath and on the right. The gaps of sky stay open.
steps.why: One move: the same brush loaded with the same golden yellow taps the mid value onto both leaf masses.

steps.name: Build the mossy rock

lays.what: a low dome right of the path, in front of the bushes: a flat-bottomed oval first, then a smaller curved piece on its right

steps.after: A low gray-green dome sits right of the path, flat at the bottom, over the bushes behind it. It is one flat color.
steps.why: The rock sits in front of the bushes and behind the near trunks.

steps.name: Shade the rock's far side

lays.what: the right side and the bottom of the rock, away from the sun

steps.after: The rock's right side and base are a cool blue-gray, curving with its shape; the gray-green top and left still show. It now looks round.
steps.why: Shadow before light, so the rock gets its three values.

steps.name: Pull the pale birch trunks

lays.what: five trunks from the bottom edge to the top: three on the left leaning a little right, the middle-left one widest, and two on the right, wide at the base and tapering up

steps.after: Five pale gray-white trunks stand from the bottom edge to the top, painted straight over the canopy, the ground and the bushes, three on the left and two on the right framing the path. They are flat, with no marks.
steps.why: The subject goes on over everything behind it, in one pale coat that the marks need to be dry before.

steps.name: Shade the right side of the trunks

lays.what: a strip down the right side of each trunk, away from the sun, darker toward the base

steps.after: Each trunk has a soft gray-brown band down its right side, heavier near the ground, and looks round; the left side stays pale.
steps.why: The shading goes under the marks, the way a teacher layers a subject.

steps.name: Lay the dark bark marks

lays.what: broken dark marks across each trunk, more and bigger toward the base, and the solid dark at each trunk's foot

steps.after: Uneven dark marks break across every trunk, some only partway, sparse and small near the top and dense near the ground, where each trunk ends in dark. The pale bark shows in big gaps.
steps.why: The dry, shaded trunk takes the marks without smearing.

steps.name: Pull the dark branches

lays.what: the main branches forking up and out from the trunks into the canopy: two from the far left trunk, one long one reaching right from the middle-left trunk, and one from each right trunk

steps.after: Thin dark branches fork from the trunks up into the gold leaves, thick where they leave the trunk and tapering to points. The leaves behind them still show.
steps.why: Lines go on last in the subject, over the dry canopy and trunks.

steps.name: Dab the shadowed fallen leaves

lays.what: dark leaf dabs over the whole ground and path, small and close at the back, bigger in front, heavier around each trunk's foot and in a few bands across the path where the trunks' shadows fall

steps.after: The ground is speckled with dark red-brown leaf dabs, thicker around the trunk feet and in soft bands across the path; plenty of rust brown and tan still shows between them.
steps.why: The leaves lie over the trunks' feet, so they come after the birches, darkest first.

steps.name: Dab the orange fallen leaves

lays.what: orange-gold leaf dabs over most of the ground and path, smaller at the back, overlapping the trunk feet

steps.after: Orange-gold leaves now cover most of the ground, over the trunk feet and across the path; the dark dabs still show between them, and the path still reads lighter.
steps.why: The mid value covers less than the dark pass and leaves it showing.

steps.name: Dab the golden fallen leaves

lays.what: golden yellow dabs over part of the orange, more on the path and on the left toward the sun, fewer on the right and in front

steps.after: Golden leaves gather along the path and the left side; the orange and dark dabs still show beneath and around them, more on the right.
steps.why: A second, lighter mid pass so the carpet builds up instead of appearing finished.

steps.name: Light the mossy top of the rock

lays.what: the top and left of the rock, facing the sun

steps.after: The rock's top and left catch a broken yellow-green moss light; its middle stays gray-green and its right side blue-gray.
steps.why: The rock's lightest value, on the sun's side.

steps.name: Catch the light on the bark

lays.what: a broken strip down the left side of each trunk, facing the sun, over some of the dry marks

steps.after: The left edge of every trunk glows near-white, breaking over a few dark marks, while the right side stays gray-brown; the trunks look round and sunlit.
steps.why: The brightest light on the subject comes near the end, on the sun's side only.

steps.name: Dab the sunlit leaves

lays.what: a few pale taps on the canopy clumps nearest the sun and on their left edges
a few pale taps on the tops of the bushes on the left of the path
scattered pale leaves on the path and on the sunlit ground on the left, fewer in front

steps.after: The finished painting: a few pale gold leaves sparkle in the canopy near the sun, on the bushes and down the sunlit path, every one on the sun's side, with the golden and orange leaves still showing all around them.
steps.why: One move: the same brush loaded with pale gold taps the sun's last light onto every leaf mass it reaches.
